mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Tuesday 4:06 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-24 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: Dell Technologies Inc
items.about: Dell sells PCs, servers, storage and the AI server systems used in data centers.
items.why: Dell fell about 12% into its fiscal Q3 report after the close, as HPE's weak outlook revived worries about AI-server margins. Posts say the results came in well above estimates (revenue near $54.9B vs about $49.3B expected, with a large AI order backlog), and the stock bounced after hours; those figures were not yet confirmed in news coverage at board time.

items.name: Strategy
items.about: Strategy is a software company that holds a large bitcoin treasury, so its shares track bitcoin closely.
items.why: Strategy dropped about 8% as bitcoin kept sliding and crypto-linked stocks sold off together. Reports earlier this month put its holdings at roughly 849,000 bitcoin at an average cost near $75,000, so the price of bitcoin relative to that cost is the main focus in the stream.

items.name: Circle
items.about: Circle issues the USDC stablecoin and earns most of its revenue from interest on the reserves behind it.
items.why: Circle fell about 7% to a new 52-week low alongside the wider crypto selloff. Posts point to heavy put buying and question whether USDC circulation is growing fast enough.

items.name: SPDR S&P Biotech ETF
items.about: An equal-weighted ETF of US biotechnology stocks, so smaller drug developers carry as much weight as large ones.
items.why: The biotech ETF jumped about 6.6%, its sharpest gain in a while, after Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $41 billion, reviving hopes of more takeovers. A string of FDA approvals over the past two days added to the move.

items.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co
items.about: HPE sells servers, storage, networking gear and hybrid-cloud services to businesses.
items.why: HPE fell about 16% after its quarterly report, as its fiscal Q1 revenue forecast of $14.0B–$14.6B came in below expectations. Posts debate whether management is trading server margin for market share; the drop also weighed on Dell and other AI-server names.

items.name: Ambarella Inc
items.about: Ambarella designs low-power AI vision chips for cars, security cameras and robots.
items.why: Ambarella fell 20% to a 52-week low as chip stocks sold off, and Morgan Stanley cut its price target to $70 from $96 while keeping an Overweight rating. Its fiscal Q3 report was due after the close; posts also mention a new edge-AI partnership with Liquid AI and an after-hours trading halt, which had not been explained in news coverage at board time.

items.name: Luckin Coffee Inc - ADR
items.about: Luckin is a Chinese coffee chain with tens of thousands of mostly app-ordered stores; its ADRs trade over the counter in the US.
items.why: Luckin's ADR rose about 3% to near $38, extending gains since its recent quarterly report. Posts are cheering the steady rise; no new company announcement was found today.

items.name: Analog Devices Inc.
items.about: Analog Devices makes analog, mixed-signal and power chips used in factories, cars, communications and data centers.
items.why: Analog Devices fell about 17% after its quarterly report: results beat estimates, but it guided fiscal Q1 adjusted EPS to about $3.82, below the $4.06 just reported, on roughly flat revenue near $4.40B. The drop came on a day when chip stocks gave back much of Monday's Nvidia-led rally.

items.name: Abercrombie & Fitch Co.
items.about: Abercrombie & Fitch sells clothing through its Abercrombie and Hollister brands.
items.why: Abercrombie jumped about 20% after a record third quarter, with net sales of about $1.4 billion, and it raised its full-year sales and earnings outlook. The rally was part of a strong day for retailers reporting ahead of Black Friday.

items.name: BlackBerry Ltd
items.about: BlackBerry sells QNX embedded software for cars and robots plus cybersecurity tools; this is its Toronto listing.
items.why: BlackBerry was flat in Toronto while its executives presented at the TD Cowen Canadian technology conference. Posts say management sounded confident about QNX margins and robotics demand; no new guidance was issued.

items.name: Sanofi-Aventis
items.about: Sanofi is a French drugmaker whose top product is the immunology drug Dupixent; these are its US-listed ADRs.
items.why: Sanofi agreed to buy Insmed for $175 a share in cash, about $41 billion, adding the lung drug Brinsupri as it prepares for Dupixent's patent expiry. Sanofi's ADRs rose about 11% on the day as the deal drew heavy chatter.

items.name: Crowdstrike Holdings Inc
items.about: CrowdStrike sells cloud-based cybersecurity software that protects computers, cloud workloads and identities.
items.why: CrowdStrike edged up about 1% a day after reporting record net new ARR of $419 million and agreeing to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued near $44 billion (1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share). The deal is expected to close in the second half of its fiscal 2028.

items.name: BlackBerry Ltd
items.about: BlackBerry sells QNX embedded software for cars and robots plus cybersecurity tools.
items.why: BlackBerry rose slightly as its CEO and CFO spoke at the TD Cowen Canadian technology conference. Posts say they talked up QNX gains in robotics and margin expansion; no new financial targets were announced.

items.name: TeraWulf Inc
items.about: TeraWulf runs bitcoin mining and builds data-center capacity leased to AI and cloud customers.
items.why: TeraWulf fell about 8% as AI-infrastructure and crypto-linked stocks slid together. Its CEO said on CNBC that nothing has changed in AI data-center demand; posts debate its multi-year lease revenue plans.

items.name: Insmed Inc
items.about: Insmed develops drugs for serious lung diseases, including Brinsupri for bronchiectasis and Arikayce.
items.why: Insmed jumped about 14% after Sanofi agreed to buy it for $175 a share in cash, about $41 billion in total. The stock closed near $170, a little below the offer price, and a law firm has announced a review of whether the price is fair.

items.name: Dicks Sporting Goods, Inc.
items.about: Dick's is the largest US sporting-goods retailer and also owns Foot Locker.
items.why: Dick's rose about 15% after fiscal Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.94 beat the roughly $1.41 estimate and revenue rose 23% to $5.13 billion. It raised its full-year EPS outlook to $11.45–$12.30.

items.name: Kohl's Corp
items.about: Kohl's runs about 1,100 US department stores selling apparel, home goods and beauty products.
items.why: Kohl's jumped about 20% after Q3 EPS of $2.15, helped by a real-estate gain, a tax benefit and tariff refunds. Comparable sales rose 1.2%, ending 18 straight quarters of declines.

items.name: TG Therapeutics Inc
items.about: TG Therapeutics sells Briumvi, an infused antibody for relapsing multiple sclerosis.
items.why: TG Therapeutics rose nearly 10% to an all-time high near $70. The FDA is reviewing its request to replace Briumvi's two-infusion start with a single 600 mg first dose, and the biotech sector rallied broadly on the Sanofi–Insmed deal.

items.name: Fuelcell Energy Inc
items.about: FuelCell Energy makes fuel-cell power plants for utilities, industrial sites and data centers.
items.why: FuelCell slid about 9%, giving back much of Monday's roughly 18% jump as fuel-cell peers Bloom Energy and Plug Power also fell. Posts complain about a lack of company news and delayed production expansion.

items.name: Verastem Inc
items.about: Verastem develops targeted cancer drugs, including a combination approved for a rare ovarian cancer.
items.why: Verastem rose about 17% on heavy volume without a company announcement, riding the sector-wide biotech rally after the Sanofi–Insmed deal. Posts note that a rival's failed pancreatic-cancer trial a day earlier raised the bar for first-line programs like Verastem's.
